original_title: Resident Evil Movie Trailer On PlayStation’s YouTube Page Is Full Of People Asking Sony To Change Course On Discs

en.title: Resident Evil Movie Trailer Ignites Fan Fury Over PlayStation Disc Ban
en.summary: A new trailer for the upcoming Resident Evil movie has become an unlikely battleground for frustrated PlayStation fans. Comments on the trailer's YouTube page are overwhelmingly focused on Sony's decision to discontinue physical game discs.
en.body:
The latest trailer for **Resident Evil: Death Island**, directed by **Eiichiro Hasumi**, has landed on PlayStation's official YouTube channel, but it's not the zombie action that's capturing attention. Instead, the comment section has transformed into a passionate protest against Sony's controversial plan to phase out physical game discs by 2028. Despite the film having no direct ties to the PlayStation brand beyond its Sony Pictures origin, fans seized the opportunity to voice their displeasure, flooding the trailer with creative and pointed commentary.

Hundreds of comments express a clear sentiment of disappointment and defiance. Many users are making light of the situation with tongue-in-cheek remarks like, "He's transporting the last physical game copy in existence" and "I cannot wait to get the physical version of this." Others reference classic survival horror tropes, with one commenter writing, "Luckily, there was an old typewriter upstairs, and he was able to save," a nod to the series' in-game save mechanics. Another user directly asked, "Leon... where are the physical discs?" The sentiment extends to current hardware, with one comment lamenting, "I love using my PlayStation 5 as a Blu-ray player." The film's tagline, "This movie looks like it's going to get physical," has also been humorously recontextualized by fans.

## Fans Rally Against the Digital Tide

This outpouring of fan sentiment underscores a broader frustration within the gaming community regarding the shift towards digital-only distribution. While Sony's decision might be driven by business logic, it clearly alienates a significant portion of its player base who value physical ownership. The existence of a petition with hundreds of thousands of signatures calling for Sony to reverse its decision speaks volumes about the emotional connection fans have to tangible media. However, industry experts suggest that Sony is unlikely to backtrack, indicating a potentially permanent shift in how games will be consumed.

## The Future of Physical Media

The **Resident Evil** movie trailer incident is symptomatic of a larger trend impacting the industry. Even major releases like **Grand Theft Auto 6** are moving away from traditional discs. Rockstar Games' upcoming title, while offering physical editions, will reportedly only include a download code, a move that has already drawn criticism, especially with reports of redemption windows, such as the 170-day limit in Japan for certain codes. This push towards digital-only or code-in-a-box solutions raises concerns about long-term game preservation and the inherent value of digital licenses compared to physical copies. As the gaming landscape evolves, the debate over physical versus digital media is far from over, and fans are making their voices heard through every available channel.

## What's Next

While the **Resident Evil: Death Island** movie trailer continues to gather comments, the focus remains on Sony's upcoming hardware and software strategies. Fans are watching closely for any further announcements or shifts in policy regarding physical media support for PlayStation consoles beyond 2028.

content_raw: The newest trailer for the upcoming Resident Evil movie from Weapons director Zach Cregger has arrived , and the version of the trailer posted on the PlayStation YouTube page is full of jokes and references to Sony's controversial decision to end support for physical game discs in 2028. The movie, which hails from Sony Pictures, doesn't have a heck of a lot to do with the PlayStation brand outside of the Sony connection, but since it was posted on PlayStation's YouTube page, people took the opportunity, and creatively, to boot, to voice their displeasure about the discs situation. The video has nearly 2,000 comments at press time. Some of the top-ranked comments read, "He's transporting the last physical game copy in existence" and "I cannot wait to get the physical version of this." Other top comments say, "Luckily, there was an old typewriter upstairs, and he was able to save" and "Leon... where are the physical discs?" Another comment reads, "I love using my PlayStation 5 as a Blu-ray player," while another states, "This movie looks like it's going to get physical." Sony's decision to end support for physical PlayStation game discs might make business sense , but it's not sitting well with fans. Hundreds of thousands of people have signed a petition calling on Sony to change course, but experts believe Sony will no go back on its decision. While Sony itself will stop supporting game discs in 2028, other companies are getting started sooner. Rockstar Games, for example, is charging $80 for GTA 6 and not releasing it on a disc . There will be physical boxes of the game sold at retail, but they only include a code, not a game disc. Even that code may not be worth anything forever, as people in Japan need to redeem it within 170 days . As for the Resident Evil movie, the film arrives in theaters on September 18. It's coming to market behind a lot of hype, considering Cregger's last two movies, Barbarian and Weapons, were big hits.
